title: Precalculus
description: A function-centered precalculus pathway through trigonometry, analytic geometry, vectors, sequences, and a limits preview; twelve teaching weeks leave three weeks for synthesis, review, and assessment.
outcomes: Analyze functions algebraically and graphically, including compositions, inverses, end behavior, and discontinuities.
Build and interpret exponential, logarithmic, and sinusoidal models in clearly defined applied contexts.
Use unit-circle reasoning, identities, inverse functions, and equations to solve trigonometric problems exactly.
Solve general triangles and reason with polar coordinates, complex numbers, vectors, and dot products.
Identify and analyze circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas from their standard equations.
Work with sequences, induction, binomial expansions, and introductory limiting behavior as preparation for calculus.

units.title: Functions, Composition, and Inverses
units.summary: Treat functions as input-output relationships and connect their formulas, graphs, and domains. Compose functions in the stated order, and find inverse values by reversing the input-output relationship rather than by mechanically taking reciprocals; remember that only one-to-one functions have inverse functions.
objectives: Evaluate functions and interpret input-output notation in numerical and graphical settings.
Compute compositions in the correct order and track the domain of each stage.
Determine inverse function values by solving an appropriate input-output equation.

units.title: Polynomial and Rational Function Behavior
units.summary: Use degree, leading coefficient, real zeros, and multiplicity to predict polynomial graphs and end behavior. For rational functions, factor before deciding whether a missing point is a hole or a vertical asymptote, and compare degrees for horizontal asymptotes; simplification does not restore excluded domain values.
objectives: Predict polynomial degree, end behavior, and zero multiplicity from factored formulas.
Distinguish removable discontinuities from vertical asymptotes using factored rational forms.
Determine horizontal asymptotes by comparing numerator and denominator degrees.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Models
units.summary: Connect exponential growth and decay with logarithms, which recover exponents and time scales. Use equivalent bases, logarithm laws, and model parameters carefully, and check candidate solutions against every logarithm's positive-input requirement before accepting them.
objectives: Evaluate logarithms and solve exponential equations by rewriting with a common base.
Interpret initial values and doubling periods in exponential growth models.
Solve logarithmic equations while enforcing all input-domain restrictions.

units.title: Angle Measure and the Unit Circle
units.summary: Measure angles in radians so that arc length, angular speed, and trigonometric definitions use a common scale. Locate terminal sides on the unit circle, use reference angles and signs by quadrant, and derive exact sine, cosine, and tangent values rather than relying on degree-mode approximations.
objectives: Relate radian angle measures to fractions of a complete revolution.
Evaluate exact sine and cosine values using unit-circle coordinates.
Combine exact trigonometric values using signs and reference angles.

units.title: Trigonometric Graphs and Modeling
units.summary: Read amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline from transformed sine and cosine formulas and connect them to graph features. In periodic models, interpret those parameters with units and check whether a horizontal or vertical shift has been applied before evaluating or predicting extrema.
objectives: Determine amplitude, period, and vertical shifts from sinusoidal formulas.
Find maximum values by combining amplitude with the midline.
Evaluate phase-shifted periodic models at specified times.

units.title: Inverse Trigonometry and Identities
units.summary: Use inverse trigonometric ranges to select the intended angle before evaluating a composition. Rearrange Pythagorean, quotient, reciprocal, and double-angle identities to transform expressions, while preserving domain exclusions and determining signs from the stated quadrant.
objectives: Evaluate compositions involving inverse trigonometric functions and right-triangle reasoning.
Use Pythagorean identities and quadrant information to determine signed trigonometric values.
Apply double-angle identities to compute exact values without finding an angle.

units.title: Trigonometric Equations
units.summary: Reduce trigonometric equations to familiar values by factoring, substitution, or identities, then account for every family created by periodicity. On a bounded interval, enumerate candidates systematically and remove duplicates at endpoints; when reporting all real solutions, include the appropriate integer-parameter family and state its restrictions.
objectives: Find a specified principal solution of a basic trigonometric equation.
Count all solutions on bounded intervals without duplicating periodic representatives.
Solve factorable trigonometric equations and count every solution in the stated domain.

units.title: Solving Triangles with the Laws of Sines and Cosines
units.summary: Match the law of sines to angle-side pairs and the law of cosines to SAS or SSS information, labeling each side opposite its corresponding angle. Include the area formula for two sides and their included angle, and analyze the SSA case explicitly because zero, one, or two triangles may satisfy the same data.
objectives: Solve for an unknown side using the law of sines with a known opposite pair.
Apply the law of cosines to SAS information without dropped signs.
Compute triangle area from two sides and their included angle.
Determine the number of triangles in the potentially ambiguous SSA case.

units.title: Polar Coordinates and Complex Numbers
units.summary: Translate between rectangular and polar coordinates with x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, and r² = x² + y², choosing angle representations appropriate to the requested quadrant. Treat complex numbers as ordered real-imaginary pairs, use i² = -1 in products, and rationalize denominators with conjugates before reading components.
objectives: Convert between polar and rectangular coordinates using trigonometric relationships.
Compute products of complex numbers and identify their real components.
Divide complex numbers by multiplying numerator and denominator by a conjugate.

units.title: Vectors and Dot Products
units.summary: Represent vectors by components and compute addition or scalar multiplication component by component. Connect magnitude with the distance formula and dot products with orthogonality and angle, keeping the distinction between a vector result and a requested scalar component or parameter.
objectives: Add vectors and report specified components of the resulting vector.
Compute squared magnitudes and dot products from rectangular components.
Use a zero dot product to determine parameters that make vectors orthogonal.

units.title: Conic Sections
units.summary: Recognize conics from standard-form equations and read off their centers, vertices, radii, axes, foci, and asymptotes. Complete the square when necessary, distinguish major-axis orientation in ellipses and transverse-axis orientation in hyperbolas, and use c² relationships appropriate to each conic.
objectives: Identify parabola vertices and circle centers or radii from standard forms.
Use ellipse parameters to locate foci along the major axis.
Determine asymptote slopes for hyperbolas in standard form.

units.title: Sequences, Induction, Binomials, and Limits Preview
units.summary: Describe sequences recursively or explicitly and distinguish term formulas from partial sums. Verify induction bases and inductive-step algebra, identify binomial coefficients alongside powers of both terms, and preview limits by simplifying a removable indeterminate form before substitution; these ideas prepare for calculus without assuming derivative rules.
objectives: Compute specified terms of arithmetic sequences from initial values and common differences.
Verify numerical instances of the algebra used in mathematical induction.
Find a specified coefficient in a binomial expansion using the binomial theorem.
Evaluate an introductory removable-discontinuity limit by factoring and substitution.
